review_evidence: Cslib/Languages/LambdaCalculus contains locally nameless and named calculi, beta/eta reduction, confluence, strong normalization, STLC/Fsub typing, and safety proofs.
Cslib/Foundations/Semantics/LTS and FLTS formalize executions, simulation, bisimulation, traces, divergence, termination, products, and categorical structure.

Cslib/Languages/CombinatoryLogic proves confluence and Church encodings; Cslib/Crypto and Cslib/Logics contain secret sharing, perfect secrecy, commitment, modal/propositional/linear logic, while Computability/Automata formalizes automata theory.
summary: Retain cslib as a broad formal computer-science library covering programming-language semantics, lambda calculi, process calculi, logic, cryptography, automata, relations, and algorithms.

review_evidence: Extracted the unit's 106-file scope from the brief into unit_files.txt (confirmed via wc -l = 106).

Byte-size sweep (wc -c) across all 106 in-scope files: zero zero-byte files. Smallest is CslibTests/CCS/VendingMachine.lean (461 bytes); largest is Cslib/Languages/CombinatoryLogic/Recursion.lean (26817 bytes).

Directory census of the 106-file scope confirms coverage spread across the library's thematic subtrees consistent with the prior review's characterization: Algorithms (CCS, Lean/MergeSort, Lean/Sort, Lean/TimeM, StatefulProcesses/DiffieHellman), Computability (Automata/DA, Automata/TwoWayNA, Circuit and Circuit/Boolean (8+6 files), Languages and Languages/Congruences, Machines/Turing/MultiTape (+Combinators, +Plumbing) and Machines/Turing/SingleTape), Foundations (Control/Monad and IsMonadHom, Data (BitString, Nat, PFunctor), Logic/Operators, Relation (5 files), Semantics/FLTS, Semantics/Frame, Semantics/LTS), Languages (CCS, CombinatoryLogic (7 files), LambdaCalculus/LocallyNameless/Untyped), Logics (HML, LinearLogic/CLL/PhaseSemantics, Modal (4 files) and Modal/Unary/Unimodal/Unimodal-Lean), MachineLearning/PACLearning, plus the CslibTests mirror suite (9 top-level test files plus CCS/Complexity/Modal subdirectories) and the two root aggregator files Cslib.lean/CslibTests.lean.

Ran a no-declaration-keyword grep (grep -LE against theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom) over all 106 in-scope files: 3 files flagged (Cslib.lean, CslibTests.lean, CslibTests/GrindLint.lean).

Read Cslib.lean in full (14350 bytes): a `module` file consisting solely of ~230 `public import Cslib....` statements, one per source module in the library, with no declarations of its own. Legitimate FILTER-007 pure-import root aggregator; retained (no verified end-to-end auxiliary delivery path exists for its navigation signal, so default retain applies).

Read CslibTests.lean in full (926 bytes): a plain file of ~30 `import CslibTests....` statements, one per test module, with no declarations of its own. Legitimate FILTER-007 pure-import root aggregator for the test suite; retained.

Read CslibTests/GrindLint.lean in full (4443 bytes): defines a custom elaborator command `open_scoped_all` via `elab ... : command => do ...`, then invokes it and a series of `#grind_lint skip <name>` and `#grind_lint check (min := 20) in Cslib` commands that exercise a linter checking `grind` annotations across the whole library for run-away instantiations. This is genuine executable/formal-adjacent content (a command elaborator plus a documented lint invocation), not a pure-import file; the earlier keyword grep missed it only because its declarations use `elab`/`#grind_lint`/`open_scoped_all` rather than the generic keyword set. Retained.

Sampled representative unflagged files across distinct subtrees to confirm genuine content beyond the grep heuristic: Cslib/Foundations/Data/BitString.lean (abbrev BitString and Boolean-function API on Fin n -> Bool), Cslib/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/DeterministicToNondeterministic.lean (embeds MultiTapeTM into MultiTapeNTM with a computation-preserving proof), Cslib/MachineLearning/PACLearning/VersionSpace.lean (version-space definition over a labeled sample), Cslib/Languages/CombinatoryLogic/Recursion.lean (general recursion in the SKI calculus), CslibTests/PACLearning.lean and CslibTests/CCS/VendingMachine.lean (concrete unit-test examples exercising the corresponding library modules). All genuine, well-documented mathematical/formal content with module docstrings and Apache-2.0 authorship headers.

No lakefile.lean or other build-config file is in this unit's scope; the 106 files are confined to the Cslib/ and CslibTests/ source trees plus their two root aggregator files, consistent with the unit's declared scope `.`.
